[Package Info](package-info.html) ::: ::: {#a38f203e .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code code-fold="true" code-summary="Show the code"} from tinytab import Table, fmt_currency, fmt_number menu = Table( { "item": ["coffee", "bagel", "croissant"], "price": [3.5, 2.25, 4.0], "sold": [120, 45, None], } ) menu.fmt("price", fmt_currency).fmt("sold", lambda x: fmt_number(x, decimals=0)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}
itempricesold
coffee$3.50120
bagel$2.2545
croissant$4.00
``` ::: ::: That's tinytab in a nutshell: a small table, with a formatter attached to two of its columns. ### Why tinytab? tinytab formats values and renders small tables, as text or HTML. It's a morsel of [Great Tables](https://github.com/posit-dev/great-tables): a few formatting functions and a very simple table class, with no dependencies. But tinytab isn't really meant to be used. It's an example: a small, complete Python package whose packaging, tests, type checking, CI, and documentation are all set up the way a real library's would be, so each part can be studied on its own and seen working together. This site is part of the example, too. ### What's on this site - **[User Guide](user-guide/introduction.qmd)**: how to use tinytab, from formatting a single number to rendering and saving tables - **[Reference](reference/index.qmd)**: every function and class, generated from the docstrings, with examples that show their real output - **[Python Packaging](packaging/index.qmd)**: the opinionated set of practices that tinytab demonstrates, covering project setup, testing, CI, code and API design, and documentation ### Installation tinytab isn't published on PyPI. Install it from GitHub: ```{.bash filename="Terminal"} pip install git+https://github.com/rich-iannone/example-python-package.git ``` The source code, with its tests and configuration, is in the [GitHub repository](https://github.com/rich-iannone/example-python-package).
